title: {{NAME}} and the Storm Over the Glimmering Keep
moral: The bravest thing you can do is trust someone else with a part of the job only they can do.

pages.content:
The sky above the Glimmering Keep had been the colour of a bruise for three days, and the fairy city inside its walls had gone very, very quiet.

The Glimmering Keep was not a place on any human map. It was built inside a valley that could only be reached by following the silver thread that unspooled from the eye of the needle star every midsummer night, and {{NAME}} had followed that thread for exactly one hour and forty minutes through a wood that smelled of cedar and faintly of lightning before arriving at the valley's lip and seeing it below.

The Keep was extraordinary, even half-submerged in the rolling dark cloud. Towers grew from crystal, each one shaped differently, some spiralled like shells, some faceted like diamonds. Bridges of woven light linked them, and the whole structure pulsed with a soft internal glow, a heartbeat made of colour.

But the cloud was swallowing it. And at the Keep's highest tower, visible for only a moment before the dark rolled over it, something was trapped.

{{NAME}} could see a horn. Pale gold, catching the last light, turning slowly.

A unicorn. Alone. At the top of a crystal tower in a storm that was getting worse.

pages.content:
The fairy waiting at the valley path was called Sable, and she was not small in the way most fairies are. She was still no taller than {{NAME}}'s fist, but she held herself like someone who had once moved a mountain and was prepared to discuss it.

'You're the one with the sun mark,' she said, studying {{NAME}}'s tunic with sharp violet eyes.

'My mum made it,' {{NAME}} said.

'The mark chose you, not the other way round,' Sable said firmly. 'It recognises something. The question is whether you do.' She darted close, hovering at eye level. 'Auryn is trapped at the top of the Seraph Tower. Auryn is the unicorn who maintains the light bridges of the Keep. Without the light bridges, the towers separate. Without the towers, the Keep falls. Without the Keep.' She stopped.

'Without the Keep?' {{NAME}} pressed.

'Without the Keep, the fairy city and everyone in it sleeps for a hundred years.'

There was a pause in which the cloud above them rumbled deeply.

'What's the plan?' {{NAME}} asked.

Sable's wings, black shot through with silver, snapped open to full spread. From somewhere behind her, a figure dropped from the cloud itself, landing with a controlled thud beside them. She was armoured in deep violet and carried no weapon, which somehow made her more alarming, not less.

'The plan,' said the armoured figure, pulling back her hood, 'is me. My name is Thren. I break things. Specifically, magical storms.'

pages.content:
They entered the Keep through the lowest crystal gate, which the storm had not yet reached, and ran.

Thren led at a pace that was just short of flying. She vaulted a collapsing light bridge without slowing, dragging {{NAME}} with one arm as they crossed on what remained of it before it dissolved into sparks behind them. Sable flew ahead, navigating by memory through corridors that were slowly going dark as the bridges failed.

'Each bridge draws power from Auryn's horn,' Sable called back, her voice sharp through the growing din of the storm. 'She's been maintaining them all alone since the storm began. She's exhausted. When she stops, they all go at once.'

The Seraph Tower's stairs were the hardest part. The crystal had begun to resonate with the storm's frequency, a sound just below hearing that vibrated in {{NAME}}'s back teeth and made his vision swim.

Thren put a hand on his shoulder. 'Focus on the step in front,' she said. 'Only the step in front.'

{{NAME}} did. And somehow the stairs ended.

The door at the top was sealed with storm-energy, crackling and dark, and Thren hit it with both palms, channelling everything she had against it. The door cracked. Then split. Then shattered in a cascade of dark sparks that fell away into nothing.

Beyond it stood Auryn, pale gold and trembling, her horn blazing with the desperate last light of every bridge in the Keep.

pages.content:
Auryn could not hold on much longer. Anyone could see it.

Her legs were shaking. Her pale gold coat was damp with effort, and her horn, still blazing, was beginning to flicker the way a candle does before it gives up entirely.

Thren assessed the situation in roughly two seconds. 'I can break the storm. But it will take everything I have and I need three minutes.' She looked at {{NAME}}. 'Someone needs to hold the bridges. Keep them running until I'm done.'

'I can't,' {{NAME}} said. 'I don't have a horn. I don't have Auryn's power.'

'No,' said Sable, landing on his shoulder and gripping his collar in both tiny fists, 'but you have the sun mark and you have your hands, and Auryn doesn't need you to do this alone. She needs you to do it with her.'

{{NAME}} looked at Auryn. She was looking back at him, those ancient eyes exhausted and afraid and, underneath the fear, hopeful in a way that made something in his chest ache.

He walked to her. He placed both hands on either side of her blazing horn, feeling the light pulse against his palms like a heartbeat that had been running too long. The golden sun emblem on his tunic blazed in response.

'I've got you,' he said. 'You're not alone.'

Auryn leaned into his hands. The bridges steadied. Thren began.

pages.content:
The storm broke like a wave that had been holding its breath for too long.

One moment the cloud was everywhere, pressing down, dark and enormous. The next it shredded outward in long silver streaks, driven back by the force of Thren's power, and the sky above the Glimmering Keep emerged, star-thick and brilliant and clean.

The light bridges blazed back to full radiance. The towers rang like struck crystal, each one singing a different note, and the sounds combined into something vast and harmonious that {{NAME}} felt in his ribcage more than heard with his ears.

Auryn stood steady. Her horn still glowed, but gently now, the way a lamp glows when nobody needs it to be a searchlight anymore. She turned to {{NAME}} and pressed her velvet forehead against his, and for one long moment they simply stood like that, breathing.

Thren sat down on the crystal floor with a graceful lack of ceremony and did not move for some time.

Sable flew slow loops above them all, saying nothing, which was its own kind of celebration.

{{NAME}} found a spot by the tower window and watched the fairy city below slowly relight itself, bridge by bridge, tower by tower, the Keep rebuilding its own brightness.

He was home and warm in bed before the last star faded, already half-dreaming.

And somewhere in the dream, Auryn's horn glowed, and Sable whispered: 'There is a second Keep, deeper in the valley, that nobody has reached for five hundred years.'
